## Context
The completed Gerrit Verified latency RCA optimized the macOS completion path, but Ubuntu jobs still occupy scarce org-wide runners for 11-14 minutes and contribute to queue contention. Follow-up questions identify three candidate levers: replace repeated Pandoc corpus rendering with static expected results plus a smaller boundary test, remove redundant work from the exhaustive 1,440-minute bridge cadence proof, and move genuinely live Jira DC coverage out of the per-change hot path while retaining fast unit coverage. This work must preserve behavioral coverage and must not use extra parallel jobs or unchanged aggregate runner usage.

## Plan
- Build a dated Ubuntu runner-time dossier from final post-remediation run 31752047186, pytest duration logs, workflow routing, and focused local runtime experiments.
- For Pandoc and render_unit, map every current assertion to the code boundary it exercises; compare static golden fixtures, a bounded real-Pandoc contract sample, and full-corpus external execution using defect-seeded experiments to detect any coverage loss.
- For the bridge cadence test, discriminate between the cost of the 1,440 arithmetic checks and invariant workflow YAML I/O; prefer hoisting invariant I/O if it preserves the exhaustive proof.
- Inventory expensive Jira DC/default-tier tests, identify which require a real Jira or external binary, and map them to faster existing or new unit contracts before proposing any lane move.
- Compare each candidate with current practice in popular actively maintained OSS projects and search tracker history for prior acceptance or rejection.
- Record a confirmed RCA and measured runner-time/wall-time savings. Create linked implementation tickets only for remediations that preserve coverage; under the operator standing approval, implement those matching OSS consensus through Gerrit.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Every Ubuntu operation or test phase over 30 seconds in the final sample is attributed to a specific mechanism and measured with a focused baseline.
- [ ] Pandoc corpus, render_unit, bridge cadence, and Jira DC lane-move proposals each have an assertion-level coverage map and an A/B runtime estimate.
- [ ] Each proposal cites tracker history and practices from popular actively maintained OSS projects.
- [ ] No accepted remediation removes an assertion, behavioral equivalence class, OS/Python cell, or external boundary; moved coverage has an explicit destination and schedule.
- [ ] Runner-minute and expected queue-pressure savings are quantified without counting parallel matrix time as critical-path wall time.
- [ ] Every consensus-backed remediation is implemented on a linked ticket, passes repository gates and Gerrit LLM-Review +1 plus Verified +1, and merges before this task closes.
- [ ] Non-consensus or coverage-risking proposals are summarized with evidence and left for operator disposition.
compiled_state.title: Reduce Ubuntu CI runner occupancy without losing test coverage
